look_here_first: Start with WOODY branches, then inspect one OPPOSITE pair of oval/elliptic (sometimes obovate) leaves. Autumn sage has relatively smooth/glabrous blades with tiny pitted glands, and larger showy two-lipped red-pink (or other cultivar-color) flowers around 25 mm long in the UT Texas treatment. Shrubby blue sage can have similarly sized leaves, but leaf surfaces are rough/hairy and its blue-purple corollas are usually smaller (often <13 mm). Flower color alone is NOT enough, especially in cultivated salvias.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small aromatic elliptic to obovate leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: showy relatively large flowers with strong color variation

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dry rocky western Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos habitat

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey's landscaping frame reinforces the mounded woody-shrub habit and flowering architecture. A second desert-field video shows a mature calyx during seed collection, adding a useful fruiting-stage cue beyond the showy corolla.

key_traits.label: Leaf dimensions
key_traits.text: UT Austin regional S. greggii blades ~8–48 × 3–22 mm, ovate/elliptic or oblanceolate with low scallops; overlaps S. ballotiflora leaf SIZE. Better check hair/texture plus the corolla.

key_traits.label: Leaf surface
key_traits.text: Leaf blades generally not coarsely hairy, minutely gland-dotted/pitted; leaf can feel smooth compared with shrubby blue sage's conspicuous rough leaf hairs. Pitted glands require true macro.

key_traits.label: Corolla
key_traits.text: In UT Austin regional description, two-lipped corolla ~25 mm long, typically scarlet/rose-red wild; cultivated varieties can be white, orange, pink and purple. Do not use garden flower color as a wild-species diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Terminal raceme with successive opposite pairs of ascending flowers, conspicuous comparatively large two-lipped lips and persistent glandular calyx.

key_traits.label: Cultivar caution
key_traits.text: S. greggii is sold in many colors and can be confused in gardens with S. microphylla and Salvia × jamensis hybrids; cultivar or hybrid flowers do NOT confirm wild S. greggii identity or native provenance.
